content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Content Trust and Image Signing in Docker"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Docker Content Trust (DCT) provides the ability to use digital signatures for data sent to and received from remote Docker registries. These signatures allow client-side verification of the integrity and publisher of specific image tags, ensuring secure software supply chains."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and Enabling DCT"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before you begin, ensure you have Docker installed and a Docker Hub account. By default, Content Trust is disabled. You can enable it for your current shell session by setting an environment variable."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"export DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST=1"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Pushing a Signed Image"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"When DCT is enabled, any 'docker push', 'docker pull', or 'docker build' command requires the use of signing keys. Build your image as you normally would and push it to your registry."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"docker build -t yourusername/my-secure-app:1.0 ."},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Now, push the image. Docker will prompt you to generate a root key and a repository key passphrase."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"docker push yourusername/my-secure-app:1.0"},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"The root key is used to sign for repository keys and represents your master authority."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"The repository key signs the specific image tags within a given repository."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Pulling a Signed Image"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"When another user or a deployment server attempts to pull the signed image with DCT enabled, Docker automatically verifies the signature against the trusted registry."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"docker pull yourusername/my-secure-app:1.0"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"If the image has been tampered with or lacks a valid signature, Docker blocks the pull operation and throws an error."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Managing Keys and Revoking Trust"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can inspect the trust data and keys associated with your repositories using the 'docker trust' command suite."},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"docker trust inspect --pretty yourusername/my-secure-app"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"If a repository key is compromised, you can revoke the signature for a specific tag to prevent others from pulling the vulnerable image."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"docker trust revoke yourusername/my-secure-app:1.0"}]
